{{Short description|American mathematician (1927–2021)}}
'''John Harris Walter''' (14 December 1927 – 20 September 2021)<ref>biographical information from Pamela Kalte ''et al.'', ''American Men and Women of Science'', Thomson Gale 2004</ref> was an American mathematician known for proving the [[Walter theorem]] in the theory of [[finite group]]s.

Born in Los Angeles, Walter received from [[California Institute of Technology]] his bachelor's degree in 1951. He received from the [[University of Michigan]] his master's degree in 1953 and his Ph.D. in 1954 with thesis ''Automorphisms of the Projective Unitary Groups'' under the supervision of Leonard Tornheim.<ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=4729}}.</ref> Walter was a visiting professor in 1960/61 and 1965/66 at the University of Chicago, 1967/68 at Harvard University, and 1972/73 at the University of Cambridge, UK. He was a professor emeritus of mathematics at the [[University of Illinois at Urbana–Champaign]],<ref>[http://www.math.uiuc.edu/directory/directory-members-department-mathematics Department of Mathematics, Directory], UIUC.</ref> where he became an associate professor in 1961 and a full professor in 1966. In 2012 he was elected a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>[https://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society], retrieved 2013-09-01.</ref> He died at the age of 93 in 2021.<ref>{{cite web |title=In Memoriam: John H. Walter |url=https://math.illinois.edu/news/2021-09-22/memoriam-john-h-walter |publisher=UNIVERSITY OF ILLINOIS URBANA-CHAMPAIGN |access-date=6 October 2021 |archive-date=2021-10-16 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211016051223/https://math.illinois.edu/news/2021-09-22/memoriam-john-h-walter |url-status=dead }}</ref>
